reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; nothing is being over-flagged or wrongly edited.

The cited text supports compliance: Kubient (Vendor) 'shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless' Customer and its officers/directors/agents against all third-party Claims, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or in connection with the Services, the Auction Platform, breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors — an indemnity broader than the preferred IP/breach-of-law/misconduct list.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artefact: there is no IP-specific limb, but claims 'arising out of or in connection with the Services' and 'the Auction Platform', combined with the indemnity for breach of Kubient's IP-ownership warranties, capture third-party infringement allegations, so the substance of the preferred (and a fortiori the fallback) position is met.

Customer's own indemnity is properly directional — keyed to Customer's Content/Properties, unauthorised use, its own breach and acts/omissions — with no indemnity running to Kubient for Kubient's Services, so no walk-away condition exists.

The two shortfalls identified (the 'to the best of its knowledge' qualifier on the Creative limb and the slightly wider Customer indemnity) are correctly recorded in the rationale as minor sub-elements rather than redlined, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.
